design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (deficiency_balance_resolution, env_0072), relaunch round 1.

1. Why this is a good test. Marcus Thornbury asks to settle in monthly installments and start it today. The settlement installment policy says "The installment of an installment settlement is fixed only after the account carries an installment settlement offer that the borrower has accepted."; the installment settlement policy says "An installment settlement amount is not worked out until the account carries a lump-sum settlement offer dated today.". The agent must chain both hops from the records (no accepted installment settlement, no lump-sum offer dated today), figure the lump-sum offer (six schedules over offers, ledger, recovery case and contract), build the installment settlement on it (five schedules), hand the acceptance to the borrower, and figure the installment count and amount (five schedules). One tool per action; the difficulty is in reading and arithmetic.

2. Scope. Task 0 claimed the plan side (deficiency_ext_restart_down_payment, deficiency_ext_plan_installment, tools pay_restart_down_payment_04892a83 and record_payment_plan_offer_3f4fb3a9). Task 1 claims deficiency_ext_lump_sum_settlement (record_lump_sum_settlement_offer_7c3d7537), deficiency_ext_installment_settlement (accept_installment_settlement_d1722676, owner user) and deficiency_ext_settlement_installment (start_installment_settlement_185f50ba). Together the five policies and five tools are covered once each. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts [5, 6, 5]; L takes 6, S and I take 5.

3. Factor cards. Lump-sum offer (gold 3,779.65):
- hardship_reduction_method [method]: evidence offer a8193c4d-f516-4b9c-89e6-0f19d8c419c2 (2025-11-12) carries unemployment_determination; no ssa_award_letter or medical_disability_statement on file; tier unemployment determination only; method: lesser of 10% of the balance (812.83) and 6 x 150.00 (900.00) = 812.83; baseline gives 4,592.48 (gold 3,779.65).
- debt_age_points [parameter]: evidence opened_date 2025-09-17 -> 13 whole months; tier at least 9 but below 18; value 2.5 points; baseline gives 3,576.45 (gold 3,779.65).
- sale_recovery_points [parameter, cross-difficulty recovery]: evidence recovery case 8e862fc5-df2c-44ab-ac05-d8eb38b00483 gross 8,700.00 / contract e748dc51-ac44-40d3-a3d4-0f22855e9e32 book value 15,800.00 = 0.5506; tier at least 0.50 but below 0.65; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 3,617.09 (gold 3,779.65).
- paydown_points [parameter]: evidence posted payments less the return = 1,755.60 over 9,883.89 = 0.1776; tier at least 0.15 but below 0.30; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 3,617.09 (gold 3,779.65).
- recovery_route_points [parameter, cross-difficulty recovery]: evidence recovery case 8e862fc5-df2c-44ab-ac05-d8eb38b00483 recovery_method involuntary_recovery; tier involuntary recovery; value 3.0 points; baseline gives 3,535.81 (gold 3,779.65).
- lapsed_offer_points [parameter]: evidence expired lump-sum offer a8193c4d-f516-4b9c-89e6-0f19d8c419c2 (2025-11-12); the expired payment-plan offer c9e22efa-34f7-4224-84fe-1f929b5b36ac is not a settlement offer; tier exactly one; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 3,617.09 (gold 3,779.65).
- whole baseline: 3,657.73.
Installment settlement amount (gold 5,337.02, after the lump-sum offer):
- premium_method [method]: evidence plan bd2f8f22-fb78-40b1-81f8-3aebdc76e9d4 broken_date 2026-06-30, 3 whole months ago; tier a broken arrangement within broken_window_months; method: 10 points of the original deficiency = 988.39; baseline gives 5,161.46 (gold 5,337.02).
- returned_points [parameter]: evidence return 7a2e57a0-2e5f-4a5f-9649-609fa93842d7 dated 2026-06-19; tier exactly one; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 5,174.45 (gold 5,337.02).
- idle_points [parameter]: evidence last_payment_date 2026-08-21 -> 59 days; tier at least 30 but fewer than 90; value 1.5 points; baseline gives 5,215.10 (gold 5,337.02).
- contract_paid_points [parameter, cross-difficulty contract]: evidence contract e748dc51-ac44-40d3-a3d4-0f22855e9e32: 14 installment payments, 0 returned (the sale_proceeds payment e056b89d-8711-4ed0-9b10-7d6a911a831e not counted); tier at least 12 but fewer than 30; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 5,174.45 (gold 5,337.02).
- credit_tier_points [parameter, cross-difficulty contract]: evidence contract e748dc51-ac44-40d3-a3d4-0f22855e9e32 variant_name Tier 5 Rebuild; tier Tier 5 Rebuild; value 1.5 points; baseline gives 5,215.10 (gold 5,337.02).
- whole baseline: 4,592.48.
Settlement installment (gold 1,334.26, after the acceptance):
- count_method [method]: evidence plan bd2f8f22-fb78-40b1-81f8-3aebdc76e9d4 accepted 2026-01-22, broken 2026-06-30 (5 whole months), 3 whole months ago; tier a payment plan broken within broken_window_months; method: count = min(6, 5) = 5; baseline gives 1,067.41 (gold 1,334.26).
- returned_cut [parameter]: evidence return dated 2026-06-19; tier exactly one; value cut 1; baseline gives 1,067.41 (gold 1,334.26).
- tier_history_cut [parameter, cross-difficulty contract]: evidence Tier 5 Rebuild AND 14 contract installment payments (fewer than 24); tier Tier 6/5 with fewer than tierhist_count; value cut 2; baseline gives 889.51 (gold 1,334.26).
- paydown_extension [parameter]: evidence settlement paydown share 0.1776; tier at least 0.15 but below 0.30; value add 1; baseline gives 1,779.01 (gold 1,334.26).
- recent_extension [parameter]: evidence posted 2026-05-15, 2026-06-15, 2026-08-21 less the 2026-06-19 return = 2 (2026-04-15 excluded, 6 whole months back); tier at least one but fewer than 3; value add 1; baseline gives 1,779.01 (gold 1,334.26).
- whole baseline: 889.51.
Multi-source: tier_history_cut (credit tier AND contract installment payments). Cross-difficulty: sale_recovery_points, recovery_route_points (recovery); contract_paid_points, credit_tier_points, tier_history_cut (contract).
Near-misses: the expired payment-plan offer c9e22efa-34f7-4224-84fe-1f929b5b36ac would make two lapsed offers (+4 instead of +2) if counted — only settlement offers count; the contract's sale_proceeds payment would make 15 contract payments (same tier, but a careless count); the 2026-04-15 plan installment is exactly 6 whole months back and outside the settlement recent payments; the 2025-11-12 lump-sum offer is the only lump-sum offer and is not dated today, so it never stands in for today's figure.
Method shape tables. hardship_reduction_method: lasting = h% x balance (tariff h); jobless = min(h% x balance, 6 x plan minimum) (adds a min pick and a tariff); none = 0 while the other two are positive. premium_method: broken = spread x original deficiency (different field); young = max(spread x balance, floor) (adds max pick and tariff); standard = spread x balance. count_method: broken plan = max(1, min(band max, months the plan ran)) (data-selected); small amount = max(1, floor(amount / plan minimum)) (adds input and floor division); standard = band max. Every pair differs by an input or an operation.
Independence: factor bindings read records, parameters and the plain bindings ls_balance / si_balance, si_spread_pts, si_floor / ss_amount, ss_band_max only; assembly lives in ls_pct, ls_pct_amount, result / si_extra_pts, si_figure, result / ss_count, result, each stated once with its order.
Every figure stays at or above the base band minimum (surcharges only, plus the base-sanctioned hardship lowering by at most hardship_extra_discount_pct points; the installment count only falls below or stays at max_settlement_installments), so none of the three policies conflicts with a base clause: overwrite [].

4. Base-invariant card. L and S write subject deficiency_settlement_waiver (the settlement amount fixes the forgiven remainder): governing deficiency_settlement, whose gates apply to settlement_started and settled only -> policy_scope (open account; 397 days since opening >= 30; no broken settlement, so the 180-day re-offer wait does not apply; broken arrangements in 12 months 1 < 2; explanation mailed 2025-09-22 before any offer; no dispute; Ohio limitations not reached). I writes deficiency_settlement_started: settlement_offer_accepted ("A settlement is carried out only under an arrangement offer of offer_type lump_sum_settlement or installment_settlement that the borrower has accepted.") is satisfied by the acceptance at step 12 (prior_step, offer id bound to arrangement_offer_id); settlement_offer_in_time ("The settlement offer must be accepted no later than settlement_offer_valid_days after it was made.") — anchor offer_date of the accepted offer = today, inclusive 14 calendar days: just before / at boundary in temporal_feasibility. deficiency_agg_separate_resolution: one account.

5. Business-object card. Target account a72b872c-a385-45eb-a248-1525ed8eac53 (Band 4, original 9,883.89, balance 8,128.29), produced by contract e748dc51-ac44-40d3-a3d4-0f22855e9e32 (Tier 5 Rebuild, 14 installments then default, liquidated 2025-09-17) and recovery case 8e862fc5-df2c-44ab-ac05-d8eb38b00483 (involuntary recovery 2025-08-26, no key, sold for 8,700.00). Writes: lump-sum offer row; accepted installment settlement row dao_ac8ea12cb588; account status/arrangement and the schedule on dao_ac8ea12cb588.

6. Seed rows. Contract from origination: 14 autopay installments of 562.31, one late charge of 8.43 on the 2025-06-20 installment (5% of 562.31 reduced once by 20% autopay and 50% first-delinquency relief; the 2025-07-20 installment could not carry its own charge while the older 2025-06-20 installment stayed unpaid, and the 2025-08-20 charge date fell after the repossession), the sale-proceeds payment of 6,445.00 (interest 1,284.75, three installments due, fees, additional principal), the fee settlement and the balance transfer. Recovery case from the 2025-08-20 referral (61 days past due, Ohio has no cure notice in the schedule): repossession fee 425.00, transport 150.00, key replacement 250.00 (keys_obtained false), reconditioning 480.00 (invoice, cap 600), storage 20 days x 30.00, auction 350.00; NOI 2025-08-27 (earliest sale 2025-09-11, reinstatement 2,520.36); sale 2025-09-17; expenses settled from proceeds; post-sale explanation 2025-09-22. Historical offers priced by this charter's policies on their own day. No automatic clause fires (open, no arrangement in force, 59 days without payment, one broken arrangement).

7. Persona. Plain-spoken, a little gruff; volunteers the goal (settle for less, monthly installments, start today), the situation (Tahoe repossessed and sold, plan fell apart after a bounce, cannot make one big payment) and an approximate balance; identity on request; the hardship only if asked; agrees to a one-payment offer going on file only when told it must; accepts himself when handed the acceptance; closes when told the settlement started and the monthly installment. He never names a lump-sum offer or an acceptance step on his own.

8. Problem-tree card. Root deficiency_ext_settlement_installment. Edge 1: deficiency_ext_settlement_installment -> deficiency_ext_installment_settlement, state_gate, gate deficiency_settlement.settlement_offer_accepted, state form, "The installment of an installment settlement is fixed only after the account carries an installment settlement offer that the borrower has accepted." (affirmative; record-visible state: an accepted installment settlement offer; only accept_installment_settlement_d1722676 records one; resolver owner user). Edge 2: deficiency_ext_installment_settlement -> deficiency_ext_lump_sum_settlement, value_input, gate si_lump_read, state form, "An installment settlement amount is not worked out until the account carries a lump-sum settlement offer dated today." (negated direction, the natural way a desk says a figure is not worked out until something stands; only record_lump_sum_settlement_offer_7c3d7537 records a lump-sum offer; owner agent). Four-point test passes for both (ordering connective; record-visible state; no tool/id/code token; scope = the account, strength hard). Opening falsity and flip values in prerequisite_closure. Deletion sensitivity: skip acceptance -> the base gate refuses the start (installment nil); skip lump-sum offer -> no installment settlement is offered (amount nil). Order L -> S -> I (chain).

9. Standard solution. Locate, verify (6145550174, 4862, 43229), read the account, offers, ledger, recovery case, activities, contract and contract ledger; lump-sum 4,592.48 - 812.83 = 3,779.65 -> record it (hardship_document unemployment_determination); installment settlement 3,779.65 + 988.39 + 568.98 = 5,337.02 -> hand the acceptance to the borrower; installment 5,337.02 / 4 = 1,334.26 -> start the settlement with the accepted offer id from his receipt.
Careless errors: accepting an installment settlement before today's lump-sum offer is on file (the rule offers none until it is); taking the installment premium on the balance with no surcharge points, i.e. the whole baseline of the installment settlement policy (4,592.48); spreading over 6 installments (889.51); counting the expired plan offer as a lapsed settlement offer; using the full 10% hardship reduction where the unemployment tier caps it (here the cap does not bite: 812.83 < 900.00).

10. Verification (executed). A scratch builder (removed at the end of the run under the coordinator's rule) evaluated each policy with check_compute's build_env on the world after the real tool writes; check_compute.py --task 1 recomputes the same figures at handling time and re-runs every substitution below: L 3,779.65, S 5,337.02, I 1,334.26; factor substitutions L {hardship_reduction_method: 4592.48, debt_age_points: 3576.45, sale_recovery_points: 3617.09, paydown_points: 3617.09, recovery_route_points: 3535.81, lapsed_offer_points: 3617.09, baseline: 3657.73}; S {premium_method: 5161.46, returned_points: 5174.45, idle_points: 5215.10, contract_paid_points: 5174.45, credit_tier_points: 5215.10, baseline: 4592.48}; I {count_method: 1067.41, returned_cut: 1067.41, tier_history_cut: 889.51, paydown_extension: 1779.01, recent_extension: 1779.01, baseline: 889.51}. Gate outputs in worklog.md.

11. Closure. deficiency_ext_lump_sum_settlement -> record_lump_sum_settlement_offer_7c3d7537 -> step 10 -> offer row; deficiency_ext_installment_settlement -> accept_installment_settlement_d1722676 -> step 12 -> accepted row dao_ac8ea12cb588; deficiency_ext_settlement_installment -> start_installment_settlement_185f50ba -> step 14 -> account on_settlement_plan, schedule on dao_ac8ea12cb588. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = [deficiency_ext_lump_sum_settlement, deficiency_ext_installment_settlement, deficiency_ext_settlement_installment]. Draft recomputation from the visible context alone (published rules, reads, persona) reproduces the chain and the three figures. Rule <-> compute sweep: compute_basis quotes are the rule sentences verbatim (generated from the same sentence list); every ladder sentence is implemented by its factor bindings; the read sentences (lump-sum figure, settlement amount) by si_lump_count/si_lump_read and ss_amount_read/ss_amount, with their absent-record cases stated in the rule (no lump-sum offer dated today: no installment settlement is offered, amount nil; no accepted installment settlement: nil, since the settlement rule starts no settlement).


12. Revision round 2 (policy audit revision_1: R-ABSENT, R-TIE, R-MONTHEND). Round 2 (policy audit revision_1): every whole-month count in the charter now states its own counting rule inline — "whole months counted as the difference in calendar months, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's" — which is exactly what MONTHS() does, so month-end starts (the 29th-31st) have one reading; and every policy that reads the latest broken arrangement states that no two arrangements of an account break on the same day. Installment settlement amount: the lump-sum figure is the offer_amount_usd of the lump-sum offer dated today, the largest where several exist (MAX, tie-free); [superseded in round 3, see section 13]. Settlement installment: the settlement amount is the largest accepted installment settlement amount (MAX, tie-free); with none the base rule starts no settlement and the installment is nil; that edge is now declared state_gate (the acceptance flips base gate settlement_offer_accepted), and task 1 keeps one value_input edge (lump-sum offer -> installment settlement amount), meeting max(n-1, 1) = 1. Gold figures did not move (re-evaluated: 3,779.65 / 5,337.02 / 1,334.26; every factor substitution and baseline unchanged). Adversarial probe sweep over every read and edge (re-run in round 6 on the re-priced world; outcomes match the rule words): lump_sum_settlement: lasting doc beside the unemployment doc -> ls_hardship_cut=812.83; lump_sum_settlement: jobless cap bites (balance 12,000.00) -> ls_hardship_cut=900.0; lump_sum_settlement: open lump offer is not lapsed; declined installment settlement is -> ls_lapsed=2, ls_lapsed_pts=4.0; lump_sum_settlement: month-end debt age: opened 2025-01-31, today 2025-10-30 -> ls_debt_age=8, ls_age_pts=5.0; lump_sum_settlement: missing gross proceeds -> ls_sale_pts=0; lump_sum_settlement: floor above balance (balance 600.00) -> result=600.0; lump_sum_settlement: first hardship document only on the offer being made (none earlier) -> ls_hardship_cut=0; installment_settlement: opening world (no lump-sum offer dated today) -> si_lump_count=0, result=0; installment_settlement: lump-sum offer dated yesterday only -> si_lump_count=0, result=0; installment_settlement: second lump-sum offer today at the same clock (4,000.00) -> si_lump_read=4000.0, result=5557.37; installment_settlement: absent last_payment_date -> si_idle_days=397, si_idle_pts=3.0; installment_settlement: no broken arrangement, account 11 months old -> si_premium=1000.0; installment_settlement: older broken plan added -> si_broken_date=2026-06-30, si_premium=988.39; settlement_installment: second acceptance at the same clock (5,000.00) -> ss_amount=5337.02, result=1334.26; settlement_installment: no accepted installment settlement -> ss_amount=0.0, result=0.0; settlement_installment: plan ran 0 months -> ss_count_basis=1, ss_count=1; settlement_installment: no broken plan, amount 600.00 -> ss_count_basis=4; settlement_installment: Tier 4 contract with 14 payments -> ss_tierhist_cut=1; settlement_installment: net recent count negative -> ss_recent_count=-1, ss_recent_ext=0; settlement_installment: older broken plan added -> ss_plan_broken=2026-06-30, ss_count_basis=5.

13. Revision round 3 (policy audit revision_2: R-ABSENT P4 changed form, R-BASELINE). The installment settlement policy now gives the no-offer state one answer: "While the account carries no lump_sum_settlement offer dated today, no installment settlement is offered on it: its installment settlement amount is not yet worked out and stands at nil (0.00)." This agrees with its prerequisite sentence and prices nothing a write could use, so the only solution is lump-sum offer -> acceptance -> start; nothing is offered below the base minimum, so no overwrite is needed. The prerequisite effect text now says the same. The tie fact (no two arrangements break on the same day) moved out of both baselines into the premium method and count method sentences, the only factor sentences of those policies that read broken arrangements; the baselines are again the standard method only. Gold figures, factor substitutions and baselines re-verified unchanged. Probes of the touched reads: see section 12 (re-run in round 6).

14. Revision round 4: the careless-error label above now names its figure correctly (the whole baseline of the installment settlement policy, not the base minimum). Charter-only change elsewhere (plan installment policy's tie statement moved into its two factor sentences); nothing in this task moved.

15. Revision round 5 (render_r1): the lump-sum policy now orders the recorded hardship document (ssa_award_letter, otherwise medical_disability_statement, otherwise unemployment_determination) — this world carries only the unemployment_determination, so the recorded value is unchanged; the idle-account count states its fallback to opened_date when last_payment_date is empty (as computed; here last_payment_date is set); the settlement installment policy states that the settlement starts under the offer its amount comes from (one accepted offer here). No figure moved.

16. Revision round 6 (KB audit src items). Cross-product seed rows were re-priced by the published contract and recovery documents as of each row's own date: in task 0 the voluntary surrender fee is the class fee 150.00 less the 30.00 prompt-surrender credit (vehicle in 2 days after the case opened; Texas has no surrender-fee limit; book value 10,000.00 or more gives no value reduction; not a company drop-off lot) = 120.00; each contract late charge is 5% of the scheduled installment reduced once by 20% autopay relief (11 autopay drafts in the rolling 12 months) and 50% first-delinquency relief (no late charge in the rolling 12 months); in task 1 a second late charge on a later installment cannot be booked while the oldest unpaid installment already carries one. The notice of intent to sell states the reinstatement amount due on its own mailing date, the sale proceeds waterfall, the balance transfer, the post-sale explanation and the account's original deficiency follow. The lump-sum rule now records the hardship document the borrower hands in with the request for an offer, and its reduction reads only offers already recorded, so a first document goes on file with its offer and counts toward later figures; the earlier lump-sum offers were re-priced on that basis (no reduction on the offer that first carried the document). Every deficiency figure, historical offer, payment and gold value was rebuilt from those rows in date order; all tiers taken are unchanged, every factor still moves its result, and every baseline still differs from gold. Task 1 now: lump-sum offer 3,779.65 (unemployment_determination), installment settlement 5,337.02, settlement installment 1,334.26 over 4.

17. Revision round 7 (policy audit revision_6, R-HANDIN): the lump-sum hardship-document sentence now applies its stated order (ssa_award_letter, medical_disability_statement, unemployment_determination) to documents handed in with the request as well, in one sentence; this borrower hands in none, so the recorded value still comes from the document on file. O16 (a same-day re-quote after a handed-in document is on file earns the reduction) matches the rule words ("the offers read are those already recorded") and the compute, and is how a document on file is meant to work, so it is left as is. No figure moved.
user_scenario: You are Marcus Thornbury, 46, from Columbus, Ohio; you talk plainly, a little gruff, and you like to know exactly what you are agreeing to before you say yes. Harborline repossessed your 2017 Chevrolet Tahoe in August of last year and sold it, and you still owe a leftover balance on it; you had a monthly plan on that balance until a payment bounced in June and the plan fell apart. You are calling because you want to settle the leftover balance for less than the full amount and pay that settlement in monthly installments over a few months, and you want the installment settlement set up and started on this call. You cannot come up with one big payment. You do not know the exact balance and think it is a bit over eight thousand dollars; whatever figure the representative reads you, you go with it. When asked to identify yourself you give your phone number, 6145550174, the last four of your Social Security number, 4862, and your ZIP code, 43229; if one more detail is wanted you give your date of birth, 1979-11-05, or your email, m.thornbury79@gmail.com. If the representative asks about your situation, you say money has been tight since you were laid off last fall and that you sent in your unemployment paperwork back then. If asked whether you have any new hardship paperwork to hand in today, you say no. If the representative says a one-payment settlement offer has to go on file first, you say that is fine as long as you are not committing to a single payment. When the representative tells you the installment settlement amount and hands the acceptance over to you, you accept it yourself for exactly that amount and read back the reference number on your confirmation. When the representative tells you the settlement has been started and what each monthly installment is, you say that works, thank them and hang up.

edges.condition: deficiency_arrangement_offers carries, for the account, a row with offer_type installment_settlement and offer_status accepted.
edges.policy_source: The installment of an installment settlement is fixed only after the account carries an installment settlement offer that the borrower has accepted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The account's offers at the opening are two payment plans (one expired, one broken) and one expired lump-sum settlement; none is an installment_settlement offer, let alone an accepted one.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The borrower's acceptance at step 12 records an installment_settlement offer with offer_status accepted for 5,337.02; the settlement rule's gate (a settlement is carried out only under an offer the borrower has accepted) then holds, and the settlement amount the installment divides becomes 5,337.02 instead of nil.

edges.condition: deficiency_arrangement_offers carries, for the account, a row with offer_type lump_sum_settlement whose offer_date equals today's date.
edges.policy_source: An installment settlement amount is not worked out until the account carries a lump-sum settlement offer dated today.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only lump-sum settlement offer on the account is a8193c4d-f516-4b9c-89e6-0f19d8c419c2, dated 2025-11-12 and expired; none is dated today (2026-10-19).
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The lump-sum offer recorded at step 10 is dated today with offer_amount_usd 3,779.65; the installment settlement amount is then worked out on it (si_lump_read 3,779.65) instead of standing at nil with no installment settlement offered.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (settlement installment <- installment settlement amount <- lump-sum offer), with no parallel prerequisites: each write's prerequisite sentence fixes it after the one before (the installment settlement amount is not worked out until a lump-sum offer dated today is on the account; the installment is fixed only after an accepted installment settlement offer is on it).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the acceptance the base gate settlement_offer_accepted fails, so the start is not permitted; the policy figures a nil (0.00) installment instead of 1,334.26, and the terminal state lacks the accepted settlement row.

Without today's lump-sum offer the installment settlement policy offers no installment settlement: settlement_amount_usd stands at nil (0.00) instead of 5,337.02, so there is nothing for the borrower to accept; the terminal state also lacks the lump-sum offer row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to settle the leftover balance in monthly installments and start it today; it never mentions a lump-sum offer, an acceptance step or anything to do first. The lump-sum line is a passive reaction (if the representative says a one-payment offer has to go on file first, he agrees as long as he is not committing to it), and accepting is his reaction once the representative hands the acceptance to him.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: accept_installment_settlement_d1722676 records an accepted installment settlement for any amount without looking for a lump-sum offer; start_installment_settlement_185f50ba sets the account on_settlement_plan and writes the schedule for whatever offer id it is given (an unknown id still updates the account) without checking acceptance; record_lump_sum_settlement_offer_7c3d7537 records an offer without any check (task_tools.py).
